metaDescription: Plan a 7-day Turquoise Coast road trip from Bodrum to Antalya along the D400 with driving tips, one-way rental fees, and coastal stops.
quickAnswer: A seven-day Turquoise Coast road trip from Bodrum to Antalya covers roughly 520 kilometres along the Muğla and Antalya coastline via the D400 highway. Split your nights across Bodrum, Dalyan or Göcek, Kaş, and Çıralı so daily drives stay under three hours, leaving daylight for Lycian ruins, boat coves, and cliffside viewpoints.
category: Turquoise Coast & Mediterranean — Antalya, Fethiye, Kaş & Gulet Cruises

body.text: What is the ideal 7-day driving route from Bodrum to Antalya?

The ideal seven-day driving route from Bodrum to Antalya breaks the 520-kilometre coastal run into four overnight bases: one night in Bodrum, two nights around Göcek or Dalyan, two nights in Kaş, and two nights in Çıralı before finishing at Antalya Airport. Keeping driving legs short avoids afternoon fatigue on winding coastal sections.
Anchor yourself in four bases rather than changing hotels nightly, treating the D400 as a slow coastal corridor instead of a transit race.

body.text: Are the D400 coastal roads difficult to drive?

The D400 coastal highway between Bodrum and Antalya is paved, well-signed, and manageable for confident drivers, though it narrows to two winding lanes between Kalkan, Kaş, and Finike. Avoid driving the cliffside stretches after dark, when unlit bends, slow agricultural trucks, and occasional loose goats demand full daylight visibility.

From Milas through Fethiye, much of the route is smooth dual carriageway. Past Kalkan toward Kaş and Demre, it becomes a winding cliffside two-lane road with limited overtaking. Refuel in Fethiye or Kaş, book a compact automatic for tight village parking, and take the steep seven-kilometre pine-forest descent into Çıralı slowly.
What are one-way car rental drop-off fees like?

One-way car rental drop-off fees between Milas–Bodrum Airport and Antalya Airport typically range from 3,850 TL to 18,750 TL depending on the agency, vehicle class, and season. According to [RentaCarSAW's October 2026 intercity fee study](https://www.rentacarsaw.com/en/blog/sehirlerarasi-arac-kiralama-one-way), drop-off charges on identical Turkish routes vary by two to four times between competing suppliers.

National chains like [Sixt Türkiye](https://www.sixt.com.tr/en/help-center/oneway-fee) price one-way returns by distance and seasonal fleet demand, while smaller local desks often refuse intercity drops in July and August. Confirm total fees and tyre-and-glass cover upfront, or compare private transfers with [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/).
Where are the must-stop viewpoints along the D400?

The finest viewpoints along the D400 sit between Kalkan and Kemer, where limestone headlands drop straight into clear Mediterranean coves. Pull only into marked lay-bys with solid shoulders, and time your stops for morning light before tour buses fill the cliffside parking strips around Kaputaş and Kaş.

items: Kaputaş Gorge Lay-By (between Kalkan and Kaş): A steep limestone canyon framing bright turquoise water; arrive before 09:30 to find roadside parking.
Kaş Panorama Bend (west approach into Kaş): Looks directly over the Antiphellos peninsula and across the strait toward the Greek island of Meis.

Patara Sand Dunes Ridge: Just inland from [Patara Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=PTR01&DistId=PTR), offering wide coastal views over twelve kilometres of protected Caretta caretta nesting beach.

Finike–Kumluca Coastal Cliffs: Sweeping bay pull-outs along the eastern approach toward [Olympos](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=OLY01&DistId=OLY) and the three ancient harbours of [Phaselis](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3FsectionId%3DPHS01%26distId%3DPHS).

faq.q: How many days do you need to drive from Bodrum to Antalya?
faq.a: Seven days is the practical minimum to enjoy the Turquoise Coast without rushing. Five days forces long stretches behind the wheel and leaves no time for a Kekova boat day or unhurried afternoons in Kaş and Çıralı.

faq.q: Is it better to drive Bodrum to Antalya or Antalya to Bodrum?
faq.a: Driving west to east from Bodrum to Antalya puts the sea on your right-hand passenger side, making pull-outs into coastal viewpoints along the D400 safer because you do not need to cross oncoming traffic.

faq.q: Do I need an International Driving Permit to rent a car in Türkiye?
faq.a: Visitors holding a Roman-alphabet licence from the UK, EU, US, Canada, or Australia can generally rent with their home licence, though carrying an International Driving Permit is strongly advised for non-Latin licences and smoother insurance verification.

faq.q: What is the best month for a Turquoise Coast road trip?
faq.a: May, early June, late September, and October deliver warm swimming temperatures, clear roads, and far lower hotel rates than July and August, when daytime heat often exceeds 36°C and coastal parking fills by mid-morning.

faq.q: Are there toll roads between Bodrum and Antalya?
faq.a: No major HGS toll motorways run along the D400 between Bodrum and Antalya; the route uses toll-free state highways, though rental cars still carry an HGS transponder in case you detour onto tolled Aegean motorways north of Aydın.

faq.q: Can I visit Kekova by car on this road trip?
faq.a: You can drive to Üçağız village, about 45 minutes east of Kaş, and board a local wooden boat there to see the sunken Lycian ruins and Simena Castle, as swimming and motorised landing over the protected ruins are restricted.
